A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lavender study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-F are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Lavender fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations and qualitative analyses for OpenFlamingo, MiniCPM-V-2.5 and Llama-3.2-11B, including supplementary results in Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the locally evaluated scores in Table 1, medical evaluation in Figure 16 and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The diffusion attention targets, aggregation options, Aligner network and combined autoregressive/MSE objective remain unchanged. Added notation and pseudocode comments do not establish a revised algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Flickr30k, Laion50k, RLAIF-V83k and OCRVQA training coverage, the same multimodal evaluation benchmarks and WorldMedQA-V. No task, domain or appendix test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Autoregressive fine-tuning remains the direct comparator. Table 1 and Figure 16 retain the same external baseline models, and the ablation comparisons retain the same alternatives.

E3.justification: Data configurations, model sizes, training budgets and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Table 1 retains VLMEvalKit with GPT-4o evaluation, while the ablations retain exact-match evaluation without an LLM judge.

E4.justification: The attention-aggregation, Aligner-pretraining and layer-selection ablations are retained. Scaling, data-overlap, failure-case and qualitative analyses in the main text and Appendix F are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including entropy summaries, Figure 14's standard-deviation shading and Figure 27's confidence intervals derived from standard errors. No run-count, seed or statistical-testing information is added.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout, including the appendices. For example, Llama-3.2-11B with Lavender LoRA retains the 90.3 DocVQA score in Table 1 and 47.0% WorldMedQA-V accuracy in Figure 16.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix B explicitly qualify the ideal-attention assumption and KL-proximity argument as applying to vision-centric tasks. This limits their stated scope; the equations and derivations themselves remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same attention-alignment contribution, efficiency claims, reported performance gains and generalisation claims.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 and Appendix B now qualify the interpretation of lower diffusion-attention entropy as supporting proximity to ideal attention specifically in vision-centric tasks. Existing failure explanations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise to share code, training data and models with an availability statement and a project-page hyperlink. This improves documented access information; hardware, hyperparameters and implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including the comparisons with VLM adapters, vision experts and existing diffusion/VLM integration approaches. The bibliography is unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits explain image/question/answer and attention-index notation, add short annotations in Appendices A and D, qualify terminology and update publication wording. Section order and almost all prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The abstract now continues into the second column, Figure 7 moves from page 7 to page 8, and existing figures are rearranged or resized. All 30 figures and three tables are retained with unchanged graphic content.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves usability through the project-page link, clearer notation and more qualified attention assumptions. A new Algorithm 2 comment about image-question pairs conflicts with Section 5's retained image-label description, creating a small documentation drawback. The overall gain is limited because the experimental evidence and mathematical derivations are unchanged.
